    mptcp: Fix out of bounds when parsing TCP options
    
    The TCP option parser in mptcp (mptcp_get_options) could read one byte
    out of bounds. When the length is 1, the execution flow gets into the
    loop, reads one byte of the opcode, and if the opcode is neither
    TCPOPT_EOL nor TCPOPT_NOP, it reads one more byte, which exceeds the
    length of 1.
    
    This fix is inspired by commit 9609dad263f8 ("ipv4: tcp_input: fix stack
    out of bounds when parsing TCP options.").

    Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

content.thinking:
The seed is clear: mptcp_get_options TCP option parsing loop — reads opsize byte without checking length >= 2, causing a one-byte OOB read. The general mechanism: variable-length option/TLV parser loops that consume a type/opcode byte and then read a length/size byte (or nested field) without validating that sufficient bytes remain in the buffer.

Now derive the mechanism profile:

- Attacker-controlled source: network-supplied packet bytes — untrusted protocol headers/options/TLVs (e.g., TCP options, IPv6 extension headers, TLV fields in netlink, wireless management frames, etc.).
- Missing guarantee: length/bound invariant — parser doesn't verify remaining buffer length before reading additional bytes of an option header (size byte, nested length, or data).
- Unsafe use: reading `*ptr++` (opsize) or copying option data when remaining length is insufficient; also potentially using the opsize to advance the pointer/copy, so insufficient checks can also lead to OOB read/write.
- Consequence: out-of-bounds read (info leak / crash), possibly OOB write if length used for copies.

Four non-overlapping search dimensions (branch names), each narrow enough for one worker in one snapshot:

1. `tcp-opt-parsers`: Other TCP option parsing loops (non-mptcp): net/ipv4/tcp_input.c, tcp_fastopen, MD5, SACK, etc. — actually tcp_input.c already had the fix; variants elsewhere. But careful: branch should be narrow. "TCP option parsers outside mptcp" — that's narrow (one protocol family).

2. `ipv6-ext-hdr-tlv`: IPv6 extension header / hop-by-hop / destination options TLV parsers (e.g., net/ipv6/exthdrs.c, MLD, RA parsing, IPv6 TLV validation functions like ip6_parse_tlv) — checking bounds before reading len byte.

3. `netlink-attr-loops`: Netlink attribute iteration loops (nla_for_each_attr style, but hand-rolled loops parsing nested/variable attributes) where remaining length not checked before reading nla_len header. Hmm, netlink is usually kernel-privileged (untrusted only if CAP), but there are user-facing ones. Maybe better: "config/packet-based TLV parsers in filesystems" — but let's stay networking-ish but also broaden.

4. `wireless-mgmt-tlv`: Wireless (mac80211/cfg80211) management frame information element parsers — beacon/probe response IEs, vendor IEs, where a 1-byte length read can exceed remaining buffer.

Alternatively, branch 4 could be "skb header pointer walkers" — generic skb_header_pointer / pskb_may_pull misuse. Or "fragment/option parsing in other L3/L4 protocols" (SCTP chunks, DCCP options, IPsec, tipc). Let me pick four:

2. ipv6-tlv-parsers — IPv6 extension-header / TLV parsers (exthdrs, MLD/RA options, ip6_parse_tlv, seg6, srh).
3. wireless-ie-parsers — mac80211/cfg80211 management-frame information-element parsing loops.
4. skb-opt-walkers-other-l4 — other transport protocol option/chunk walkers (SCTP chunk/param parsing, DCCP options, TIPC, MPTCP-adjacent path-manager PM/addr parsing). 2. ipv6-ext-hdr-tlv: IPv6 extension headers & neighbor discovery option TLVs (exthdrs.c, ndisc.c, ip6_flowlabel, seg6, MLD reports).

content.text: {"event":"done","description":"Mechanism profile: SEED MECHANISM — a variable-length option/TLV parser walks an attacker-controlled wire buffer in a loop. It consumes the opcode byte first, then (for any opcode that is not the 1-byte padding kinds EOL/NOP) dereferences the next byte to obtain the option size, without first verifying that at least 2 bytes of the option space remain. Untrusted source: bytes of protocol options/TLVs carried in remotely receivable packets (no auth, no integrity check before parse). Missing guarantee: a length-bound invariant — 'every byte read inside iteration i must lie within the remaining validated length' is never asserted before the size-byte read (and analogous parsers also skip checks before following the size field with a data read or pointer advance). Unsafe use/state transition: read past the end of the option area (stack or skb data) via '*ptr++' after decrementing length for the opcode only; sibling forms include trusting a length field to bound a memcpy/memcmp or to advance the cursor, enabling both OOB reads and, where lengths drive copies, OOB writes. Consequence: out-of-bounds read of adjacent memory (info disclosure into later packet echoes/logs or crash/DoS). Transferable invariant: in any loop that parses variable-length records from an untrusted buffer, the code must re-validate remaining >= header size before reading each header field (type, then size, then payload) and before advancing; absence of the 'remaining >= 2' style check right before the size-byte deref is the bug signature. The seed (net/mptcp/options.c mptcp_get_options) is a demonstration only and must never be reported. BRANCHES: branch1=tcp-opt-parsers (all TCP-option walking loops outside net/mptcp: net/ipv4 & net/ipv6 tcp option parsing, fastopen/SACK/MD5/timestamp/syncookie and any duplicated option-loop copies, checking each opcode/deref against remaining length); branch2=ipv6-ext-hdr-tlv (IPv6 extension-header and ND/TLV parsers: exthdrs.c, ip6_parse_tlv-style walkers, hop-by-hop/destination options, router/neighbor discovery option TLVs, seg6/SRH sub-TLVs — bounds checks before reading each TLV len byte and before len-driven copies); branch3=wireless-mgmt-ie (cfg80211/mac80211 management-frame information-element parsers: beacon/probe/assoc request/response IE loops, vendor and extension IEs, mlme/rx handlers — whether the IE length byte is read only after confirming remaining bytes and whether ie_len/remaining bookkeeping is consistent); branch4=sctp-dccp-option-loop (net/sctp chunk/parameter/TLV walkers and net/dccp option-loop parsing: whether each chunk/parameter header read and length-driven cursor advance or copy is preceded by an end-of-buffer check); complete:false}
